textbookBox.concept: The perimeter of a closed plane figure is the distance covered along its boundary when we go around it once. For a polygon it is the sum of the lengths of all its sides.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 maths · Perimeter and Area · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Area is the amount of surface inside a closed figure. We measure it by counting unit squares that cover the figure without gaps or overlaps. A unit square of side 1 cm has an area of 1 sq cm.

beats.en: Area is the amount of surface inside a closed figure. We measure it by counting unit squares that cover the figure without gaps or overlaps. A unit square of side 1 cm has an area of 1 sq cm.
beats.speakEn: Area is the amount of surface inside a closed figure. We measure it by counting unit squares that cover the figure without gaps or overlaps. A unit square of side 1 centimetres has an area of 1 square centimetres.

beats.en: Many shapes are not rectangles, but we can cut them into rectangles, find each area and add. An L shaped figure is split into two rectangles in this way. We can also subtract.
beats.speakEn: Many shapes are not rectangles, but we can cut them into rectangles, find each area and add. An L shaped figure is split into two rectangles in this way. We can also subtract.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 maths · Perimeter and Area · Exam Challenge
textbookBox.concept: A rectangular park is 70 m long and 45 m wide. How much will it cost to fence it with 3 rounds of wire at ₹12 per metre? (Enter rupees)
textbookBox.example: Perimeter (1 round) = 2 × (70 + 45) = 2 × 115 = 230 m. Total wire for 3 rounds = 3 × 230 m = 690 m. Total cost = 690 × ₹12 = ₹8,280.

2.tip: Watch out for common exam traps — double-check units, labels, and signs!
